'''Amolak Chand Jain''' (27 December 1928 – 23 May 2021) was an Indian [[natural product chemistry|natural product chemist]], academic and the head of the department of chemistry at [[Delhi University]], [[University of Jammu]] and [[Himachal Pradesh University]].<ref name="Indian fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N81-0333 |title=Indian fellow |date=2016 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=5 November 2016 |archive-date=11 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161111061325/http://insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N81-0333 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He is known for his studies on [[polyphenols]], [[flavonoids]] and [[isoflavonoids]] and their syntheses.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/content/Detail.aspx?AID=480 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2016 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |access-date=5 October 2016}}</ref> He is an elected fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]] and the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]]<ref name="NASI fellows">{{cite web | url=http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=J | title=NASI fellows | publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India | date=2016 | accessdate=9 November 2016 | archive-date=7 July 2020 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200707200112/http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=J | url-status=dead }}</ref> and a life member of the International Academy of Physical Sciences.<ref name="Life member - IAPS">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iaps.org.in/web/index.php/2014-07-09-04-26-17/2-uncategorised |title=Life member - IAPS |date=2016 |publisher=International Academy of Physical Sciences}}</ref> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1969, for his contributions to chemical sciences.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | accessdate=5 October 2016}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Amolak Chand Jain, born on 27 December 1928 to Jugal Kishore Jain and Kala Wati in the Indian capital of Delhi, graduated in chemistry (BSc hons) in 1948 from the [[University of Delhi]] and passed his master's degree from the same university in 1950.<ref name="Indian fellow" /> After a brief stint as a research assistant at his alma mater, he started his career as a lecturer in 1952 at the department of chemistry and did his doctoral studies under the guidance of [[T. R. Seshadri]], a renowned chemist and [[Padma Bhushan]] recipient, to secure his PhD in 1954. Moving to [[Cambridge University]] in 1956, he did researches on [[Chlorophyll|chlorophyll synthesis]] at the laboratory of [[George Wallace Kenner]], a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]], and secured another PhD in 1958. He returned to India the same year to resume his career at Delhi University and continued his researches on a senior research fellowship from the [[Indian National Science Academy]]. While serving as a reader from 1961, he received a UNESCO fellowship in 1966 which assisted him to continue his researches in Moscow which earned him the degree of Doctor of Science in 1967. Two years later, he was appointed as a professor and head of the department of chemistry at the [[University of Jammu]] where he stayed till 1973 when he moved to [[Himachal Pradesh University]] as the head of the chemistry department there. In 1978, he returned to Delhi University where he spent the rest of his career. In between, he had short stints at [[Texas Agricultural and Mechanical University]] (1986), [[Budapest University]] and [[University of Mauritius]] (1989–90) as a visiting professor.<ref name="Indian fellow" />

Working on [[polyphenols]] early in his research career, Jain elucidated the structure of several compounds in natural products.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=1999 | accessdate=5 October 2016 | pages=34 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304043957/http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | archive-date=4 March 2016 | url-status=dead | df=dmy-all }}</ref> It was during this period, he worked on the [[biogenesis]] of [[chlorophylls]] and developed new protocols for the synthesis of polyphenols. Later, he focused on the chemistry of [[flavonoids]] and [[isoflavonoids]] and is reported to have achieved the synthesis of a number of such products. He has published his research findings by way of over 275 articles published in peer-reviewed journals{{Refn|group=note|Please see ''Selected bibliography'' section}} and has authored a text book on organic chemistry. He guided 30 MPhil and 30 PhD students in their studies.<ref name="Indian fellow" /> He is also associated with Indian Science Abstracts journal as a member of its editorial board.<ref name="Editorial Board">{{Cite web |url=http://www.niscair.res.in/sciencecommunication/abstractingjournals/isa.htm |title=Editorial Board |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Science Abstracts}}</ref>

A senior scientist of the Indian National Science Academy from 1995 to 2000, Jain contributed to the restructuring of academic courses during his tenure at Delhi University from 1985 to 1991.<ref name="Indian fellow" /> He is a life member of the International Academy of Physical Sciences,<ref name="Life member - IAPS" /> [[Indian Chemical Society]], [[Indian Science Congress Association]]<ref name="ISCA life member">{{Cite web |url=http://www.sciencecongress.nic.in/html/life_members.php |title=ISCA life member |date=2016 |access-date=10 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161108000435/http://sciencecongress.nic.in/html/life_members.php |archive-date=8 November 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and the [[Chemical Research Society of India]].<ref name="CRSI life member">{{Cite web |url=http://www.crsi.org.in/index.php/life-member/individual-members/97-life-member-j |title=CRSI life member |date=2016 |publisher=Chemical Research Society of India |access-date=10 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161114124732/http://www.crsi.org.in/index.php/life-member/individual-members/97-life-member-j |archive-date=14 November 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was a UGC National Professor in 1976 and is an elected fellow of the Indian National Science Academy and the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]].<ref name="NASI fellows" /> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] awarded Jain the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1969.<ref name="Chemical Sciences">{{cite web|url=http://www.csir.res.in/External/Heads/career/award/BPRIZE/CHEMICAL_SCIENCES.htm |title=Chemical Sciences |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research |date=2016 |accessdate=7 November 2016 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120912012851/http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/career/award/BPRIZE/CHEMICAL_SCIENCES.htm |archivedate=12 September 2012 }}</ref> The University of Delhi have instituted an annual scholarship, ''Professor A. C. Jain Fellowship'', to recognize academic excellence in organic chemistry among post-graduate students.<ref name="Professor A. C. Jain Fellowship">{{Cite web |url=http://www.du.ac.in/du/uploads/scholarships/scan/Dept/21082014_dept_67.pdf |title=Professor A. C. Jain Fellowship |date=2016 |publisher=Delhi University}}</ref>

Jain died on 23 May 2021, at the age of 92.<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor A C Jain |url=https://insajournal.in/intranetinsa/deceased_detail.php?id=N81-0333 |website=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=9 January 2024}}</ref>
